# TSK-603 — Journal Entry approval

Status: blocked — Computer Use acceptance capability unavailable

## Goal and approved policy

Implement one native Frappe Workflow for every standard ERPNext `Journal Entry`:

`Draft → Pending Review → Reviewed → Approved → Submitted → native GL`

The owner confirmed the route on 2026-09-26. `Accounts User` is Maker, `Accounts Manager` is
Checker, and `C-Level Approver` is Final Approver. The three protected actors must be distinct.
There is no voucher-type, `is_system_generated`, import, API, RPC, or background-submit bypass.
Journal Entries generated by native ERPNext, HRMS, or ERPNext Thailand must remain drafts and enter
the same Workflow when their source previously attempted immediate submission; they must not post
GL until approved and submitted through the Workflow.

This task does not create an accounting request DocType, approval engine, delegation engine, or GL
posting implementation. ERPNext/ERPNext Thailand remain the Journal Entry controller and ledger
owners.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every new Journal Entry starts in `Journal Entry Draft`; only the Workflow can reach a submitted
  state.
- Maker may Send and Resubmit. Checker may Review or Return. Final Approver may Approve, Return, or
  Reject. Accounts Manager may Submit after approval and Cancel after submission.
- Maker, Checker, and Final Approver are distinct canonical User identities even when one User has
  several roles or an Employee identifier is encountered.
- Review and Approve atomically capture the acting Employee, action time, and approval-signature
  value. Native Version, Workflow Action, and Timeline remain the event history.
- Approval binds to a versioned deterministic digest of every posting-critical parent and account
  row value. A critical edit after Review is rejected until Return clears the current approval
  evidence and the Maker resubmits.
- UI, REST/RPC, import, direct `Document.submit()`, background submission, and forged workflow state or
  snapshot values cannot create GL without current persisted approval evidence.
- Return and Reject remain draft and create no GL. Approved Submit invokes the installed Thailand
  subclass and native ERPNext validation/posting exactly once.
- Native generators create/link a draft rather than failing or silently claiming a posted result.
  Their source document must not report a posted accounting effect before the Journal Entry is
  approved and submitted.
- Native cancel/amend/reversal behavior remains authoritative. Cancellation is exposed only by the
  Workflow transition and does not create a custom reversal.
- Existing TDS blocking and ERPNext Thailand petty-cash/tax behavior do not regress.

## Workflow matrix

| Current state | Docstatus | Action | Role | Next state | Next docstatus | Snapshot |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| Journal Entry Draft | 0 | Send Journal Entry for Review | Accounts User | Journal Entry Pending Review | 0 | Maker |
| Journal Entry Pending Review | 0 | Review Journal Entry | Accounts Manager | Journal Entry Reviewed | 0 | Checker |
| Journal Entry Pending Review | 0 | Return Journal Entry | Accounts Manager | Journal Entry Returned | 0 | clear |
| Journal Entry Reviewed | 0 | Approve Journal Entry | C-Level Approver | Journal Entry Approved | 0 | Approver |
| Journal Entry Reviewed | 0 | Return Journal Entry | C-Level Approver | Journal Entry Returned | 0 | clear |
| Journal Entry Reviewed | 0 | Reject Journal Entry | C-Level Approver | Journal Entry Rejected | 0 | none |
| Journal Entry Approved | 0 | Return Journal Entry | C-Level Approver | Journal Entry Returned | 0 | clear |
| Journal Entry Returned | 0 | Resubmit Journal Entry for Review | Accounts User | Journal Entry Pending Review | 0 | none |
| Journal Entry Approved | 0 | Submit Journal Entry | Accounts Manager | Journal Entry Submitted | 1 | none |
| Journal Entry Submitted | 1 | Cancel Journal Entry | Accounts Manager | Journal Entry Cancelled | 2 | none |

Rejected Journal Entries have no outgoing transition. Correction uses Return; a rejected document
is retained as audit history and a new/amended draft follows native behavior.

## Digest contract

The stored value is `je-approval-v1:<sha256>`. Review also stores
`approval_digest_schema`, canonical JSON containing the v1 parent/row fieldnames, each numeric
field's resolved precision, the sorted enabled Accounting Dimension fieldnames, and the installed
Thailand fieldnames included in v1. The hash input is UTF-8 canonical JSON with sorted object keys,
compact separators, explicit nulls, dates in ISO format, checks/integers as integers, and
currency/float values normalized as decimal strings using the field precision. Account rows remain
in their persisted `idx` order; row order and row addition/removal are critical changes.

Parent fields include company, posting date, voucher type, finance book, multi-currency/opening
flags, cheque/bill/due-date references, inter-company/deferred/reversal/payment/stock links,
payment mode, write-off controls, tax-withholding controls, remarks that flow to GL, and installed
ERPNext Thailand tax controls proven to affect submit behavior. Derived display-only totals, title,
letter head, and print settings are excluded.

Account rows include account, party, currency/exchange rate, debit/credit in account and company
currency, reference type/name/due date/detail number, advance/bank flags, project, cost center, all
enabled Accounting Dimension fieldnames, row remark/against account, and installed Thailand tax and
petty-cash fields proven to affect GL/tax behavior. The runtime builds the payload from a closed v1
field allowlist plus the current enabled Accounting Dimension registry. Review, Approve, and Submit
resolve the registry independently and require it to equal the stored schema byte-for-byte. A newly
enabled/renamed dimension, changed numeric precision, or changed v1 Thailand registry invalidates
the approval and requires Return/re-review. An unrelated unknown field remains explicitly
non-critical until a reviewed v2 adds it; it is not silently promoted into v1.

Adding a new posting-critical field requires a new digest version and compatibility decision.

## Native-generator compatibility

An active Workflow changes native generator behavior. Before implementation, tests must pin each
installed direct generator identified in the source audit: Payroll Entry accrual and Bank/Cash
payment, depreciation/asset disposal/reversal, Asset Value Adjustment, deferred accounting,
exchange gain/loss and revaluation, Payment Order, Bank Reconciliation Tool, Invoice Discounting,
Share Transfer, Employee Advance, Full and Final Statement, ERPNext Thailand petty cash, and Thai
undue-tax helpers.

Do not trust a client-set `voucher_type`, remark, `is_system_generated`, hidden field, or document
flag as a bypass. Where an installed generator already checks for an active Workflow, retain its
native draft behavior. A generator that calls `submit()` directly needs an app-owned, source-specific
adapter using the documented Frappe override mechanism; the adapter creates the same native Journal
Entry as a draft, preserves its source link, and does not report a posted result. Third-party source
files are read-only.

The route was decomposed into three serialized child gates. Activation on the disposable test site
occurred only after the core, generator-adapter, and migration-readiness reviews passed:

1. `JE-CONTROL-CORE` implements the workflow guard, digest, snapshots, state-transition proofs,
   collision preflight, inactive fixture, and focused lifecycle tests.
2. `JE-GENERATOR-ADAPTERS` pins every installed generator in the matrix below and implements the
   exact source adapter or native-draft assertion. It may not activate the Workflow.
3. `JE-ACTIVATION` merges the serialized fixture/hook/setup files, activates the reviewed route on
   `local.test`, runs migration/recovery and full automated gates, then performs Computer Use.

### Installed generator matrix

| Source | Installed behavior | App-owned contract | Adapter surface |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Payroll Entry accrual | saves with `ignore_permissions`, then direct Submit; links JE to Salary Slips | retain Salary Slip link to a draft; Payroll Entry must expose pending accounting rather than claim GL | `extend_doctype_class` mixin for `Payroll Entry.make_journal_entry` |
| Payroll Entry Bank/Cash payment | same helper, normally creates draft | retain native draft and source references | Payroll Entry mixin contract test; no behavior override unless installed source changes |
| Depreciation/Asset Disposal | already skips Submit when a Workflow exists | retain native draft and Asset/depreciation links | source/integration test; no override |
| Reverse depreciation on restore | native source rejects an active JE Workflow | preserve the native rejection and prove no reversal GL; enablement records this native limitation rather than fabricating a reversal | `restore_asset` and parent integration tests; no override |
| Asset Value Adjustment | direct Submit, then stores JE link | create draft and store the same link; do not claim GL | `extend_doctype_class` mixin for `Asset Value Adjustment.make_asset_revaluation_entry` |
| Deferred accounting | saves/directly submits and commits per item | persist one linked draft per source item, avoid duplicate drafts on retry, and do not advance booked-through evidence until GL exists | JE extension recognizes the trusted `process_deferred_accounting` link; generator integration test owns retry/status semantics |
| Exchange gain/loss and revaluation | native helpers create generated JE | retain one draft with native source/reference fields; no GL until Workflow Submit | JE extension plus source integration tests; no module monkey-patch |
| Payment Order | already saves a draft | retain native draft and `payment_order` link | source/integration test; no override |
| Bank Reconciliation Tool | direct Submit then calls `reconcile_vouchers`, which allocates the Bank Transaction | lock the Bank Transaction; reuse one draft by source provenance; return the unchanged Bank Transaction plus draft JE link; do not call `reconcile_vouchers` until approved JE submission | `override_whitelisted_methods` for `create_journal_entry_bts` in `journal_entry_generators.py` |
| Invoice Discounting | whitelisted `create_disbursement_entry` / `close_loan` return unsaved JEs and do not Submit | retain returned draft and `Invoice Discounting` row references | source/integration tests; no override |
| Share Transfer | whitelisted `make_jv_entry` returns an unsaved JE dict | retain the native user-reviewed draft path | source/integration test; no override |
| Employee Advance return | returns an unsaved JE dict | retain the native user-reviewed draft path | source/integration test; no override |
| Full and Final Statement | returns a JE document | retain the native draft path | source/integration test; no override |
| ERPNext Thailand petty cash | whitelisted save/direct Submit and UI success; Petty Cash Holder balance is GL-derived | require a client operation UUID, lock the Petty Cash Holder, reuse the draft with the same operation UUID, return its link, leave GL-derived balance unchanged, and show pending approval rather than completed top-up/withdrawal | `override_whitelisted_methods` plus app form script in `journal_entry_generators.py` / `public/js/petty_cash_holder.js` |
| Thai undue-tax helper | returns a JE without submitting in the inspected path | retain native draft and `for_payment`/tax rows | source/integration test; no override |

If a source audit disproves any row, the child reports scope expansion and the primary updates this
complete matrix and exact files before its implementation. No generator receives an implicit
allowlist or an approval bypass.

## Server execution contract

`connect_diagnostics_core.api.erpnext.journal_entry_workflow` is registered through `doc_events`:

- `validate` rejects critical changes when the persisted state is Reviewed or Approved;
- `before_submit` locks and reads the persisted Journal Entry, then requires persisted Approved,
  in-memory Submitted, current digest/snapshots/actors, current submit permission, and a valid
  server-signed Submit transition proof before the installed Thailand `on_submit`/native GL path;
- `before_cancel` locks and reads the persisted submitted Journal Entry, then requires in-memory
  Cancelled, current cancel permission, and a valid server-signed Cancel transition proof before
  native cancellation;
- cleanup clears request-local execution markers on failure.

The Submit and Cancel Workflow transitions each run a synchronous transition task before native
`apply_workflow()` calls `doc.submit()` or `doc.cancel()`. The task creates an HMAC proof bound to
action, site, DocType/name, digest, persisted source state, target state, and canonical actor using
the site-scoped encryption key. The task locks the persisted Journal Entry, verifies the exact
Approved (Submit) or Submitted (Cancel) source state, and uses `db_set(update_modified=False)` to
write the proof while leaving that persisted workflow state unchanged. It must then set the
identical proof, actor, digest, and schema values on the same in-memory `doc` object passed to the
transition task. The proof field is hidden/read-only/no-copy. The installed Journal Entry metadata
has `queue_in_background = 0`; Submit and Cancel therefore remain synchronous native Workflow
operations. Background workers, imports, RPC calls, and other direct callers have no request-local
Workflow marker and fail closed. No Submission Queue exception and no custom posting or
cancellation method is introduced.

For synchronous Workflow execution, the same proof is persisted by the transition task and consumed
by the guard in the one request transaction. A request-local execution marker is single-use and
bound to the proof; direct `Document.submit()`, whitelisted submit, REST/RPC, import, or a forged
target state has neither a valid single-use marker nor a valid proof sourced from an allowed
transition. The locked persisted state must be exactly Approved for Submit and Submitted for Cancel;
Draft, Pending Review, Reviewed, Returned, Rejected, stale proofs, copied proofs, and a second call
all fail before native `on_submit`/`on_cancel`.

Use `extend_doctype_class`, not `override_doctype_class`, for the small Journal Entry submission
extension so the runtime base remains `erpnext_thailand.custom.journal_entry.JournalEntry`. The
extension may turn only the matrix's proven native generator attempts into a saved draft; direct
Desk/API/import calls proceed to the guard and fail. Generator-specific source state is handled by
the named adapter, never by a broad Submit exception.

## Migration and recovery

Preflight on `local.test` and every target site:

- stop if any active Journal Entry Workflow other than the exact owned configuration exists;
- stop if the owned name exists with another DocType, unknown states/transitions/tasks, or a changed
  fingerprint;
- stop for incompatible Custom Fields or transition-task definitions;
- report draft/submitted/cancelled Journal Entries and open Workflow Actions before activation;
- on the currently verified empty `local.test`, install additive fields/tasks and allow fixture sync.

The patch performs every collision and pending-document preflight before its first write. It creates
additive fields and exact transition-task records only; every write is idempotently validated before
reuse. On the verified empty site there is no prior JE Workflow to restore. A collision site is left
unchanged and receives a machine-readable preflight report for owner disposition. A partial failure
is recovered by rerunning: exact owned fields/tasks are reused, conflicts stop, and no history is
deleted. Unit and migration-rehearsal tests inject failure after fields and after each task.

Repeated migrate must converge without overwriting site-owned records. Recovery is non-destructive:
preserve Workflow Action, Version, Timeline, snapshots, and submitted/cancelled documents. Never
remove the guard while an in-flight governed Journal Entry remains unresolved.

## Automated evidence

Focused unit/integration tests on `local.test` cover:

- balanced happy path with three distinct actors and one native GL set;
- maker Send/Resubmit and denied Review/Approve; checker denied Approve; multi-role bypass denied;
- missing Employee/signature and revoked document permission;
- REST/RPC/direct submit/import/background-submit/state/snapshot/proof spoof attempts, proof replay,
  copied proof, and a second submit/cancel in the same request;
- Return/Reject no GL and snapshot reset;
- mutation of every digest category and one explicitly non-critical field;
- duplicate/retry and concurrent Submit: one transaction wins; the loser receives the native
  already-submitted/conflict result; exactly one voucher and GL set exist;
- native cancel, amend, and reversal behavior;
- enabled Department/Territory dimensions and multi-currency;
- every installed generator contract listed above;
- current TDS and ERPNext Thailand validation hooks.

Final gates are the pinned pre-commit command and the relevant/full app test commands on
`local.test`. Computer Use then demonstrates Maker → Checker → Approver → Submit/GL,
Return/Resubmit, denied self-approval, cancellation, and Timeline/Workflow Action evidence through
`dev.erp.connectdiagnostics.test` using test-only data.

Migration rehearsal on the empty `local.test` was independently marked READY, backed up, and run
three times successfully. Runtime integration uses the active fixture and real
`frappe.model.workflow.apply_workflow`: three distinct actors reached native Submit and two native
GL rows, then Workflow Cancel; direct Administrator submit, multi-role self-review, Return/Resubmit,
Reject/no-GL, and post-Review mutation were also exercised. The test identified and fixed Frappe
User Permission filtering on Employee snapshot links by marking audit links to ignore user
permissions.

The pinned pre-commit gate passes. Focused tests pass with 38 unit and four real integration tests.
The full-app command was also attempted; the repository-wide Frappe runner lost
`frappe.local.site` while moving from the unit category to the integration `before_tests` hook and
reported 20 `AttributeError: site` errors. The independent reviewer found no TSK-603 defect in that
failure and marked the final code review READY with no P0/P1/P2 findings.

Computer Use acceptance is blocked on the current Codex host because it exposes no browser-control,
Chrome-profile, desktop-screenshot, or screen-recording capability. The browser tester did not open
the Desk, mutate test data, or claim a UI pass; test users/roles, host reachability, served-worktree
identity, visible actions, and video evidence therefore remain unverified. Repeat the Computer Use
gate from a ChatGPT desktop host with those capabilities before promotion. Generator adapter unit
contracts pass; broader source-document lifecycle acceptance remains part of that runtime gate.

## Documentation

Only after automated and Computer Use acceptance, create
`docs/accounting/journal-entry/README.md` and update `docs/accounting/behavior.md`. The final docs
describe accepted current behavior only. An independent reviewer compares them with code and
runtime evidence before acceptance.

## Rollback boundary

Rollback does not cancel or reverse accounting entries and does not fabricate history. Native
Journal Entry cancel/amend/reversal owns accounting recovery. The active route is confined to the
disposable `local.test` validation site; do not promote it to another environment until Computer Use
acceptance completes. Retain the task evidence until the blocker is resolved.
